pr_title: fix ping with SendIpHeader on FreeBSD
pr_body:
Contributes to #14537

It seems like OS X expects length in host byte order while freebsd does not. 

cc: @Thefrank

> It seems like OS X expects length in host byte order while freebsd does not.

This is correct with being FreeBSD version dependent:
```
     Before FreeBSD 10.0 packets received on raw IP sockets had the ip_hl subtracted from the ip_len field.

     Before FreeBSD 11.0 packets received on raw IP sockets had the ip_len and ip_off fields converted to host byte order.  Packets written to raw
     IP sockets were expected to have ip_len and ip_off in host byte order.
```
https://www.unix.com/man-page/FreeBSD/4/ip/

P.S.
There is also OpenBSD which behaves differently :)

Since this did not get any traction (yet?) I decided to push more fixes:
- I added version check we discussed with @sakno (fixes #63530)
- fix DF bit handling - FreeBSD needs different order once again
- change test buffer size for FreeBSD. 
ping utility fails with `ping: packet size too large: 198 > 56: Operation not permitted`. We surface this as `Timeout` and some tests were failing. It may be _nice_ to surface better error (perhaps other platforms too) but I did not want to make this any bigger.

`/sbin/ping6 -c 1 -x 1000 -s 16 ::1` will work under FreeBSD 12.3 (or lower)
`/sbin/ping6 -c 1 -W 1000 -s 16 ::1` will work under FreeBSD 13.0+

yes, PING changed between FreeBSD 12 and FreeBSD 13


`Merged the ping(8) and ping6(8) utilities. ping(8) supports both IPv4 and IPv6. A legacy ping6(8) is retained for backwards compatibility. 3cde9171d2d5`

legacy version does not take legacy options and args though which the error being encountered here [maybe?]

Just to add: this was confusing because the first line works fine on my production FreeBSD 12.3 machine but fails on my test VM (13.0). This is even more confusing for people [me] who have used FreeBSD for a long time and don't have time to read every line of the release notes to see how a long standing utility got dramatically changed

OMG, that looks like breaking change in `ping6` utility. Unfortunately, I was unable to predict that behavior. PR was merged more than year ago. @wfurt , we need to have both versions of FreeBSD in Azure DevOps pipeline for .NET Runtime.

Here is the code:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a9c5eadd951dcba73167f72cc624eb790573663a/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Net/NetworkInformation/UnixCommandLinePing.cs#L91-L101

`OperatingSystem.IsFreeBSD()` is not enough anymore. Probably, `Environment.OSVersion` could help. However, on my Linux machine, [OperatingSystem.Version](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.operatingsystem.version) property returning a kernel version, not a version of a distribution (Ubuntu in my case). `ping`/`ping6` are user-mode programs and loosely coupled with kernel version. I think the same situation on FreeBSD. So checking version via `Version` property can be potentially dangerous.

yeah. It is really unfortunate that the syntax changed. and since we don't have regular tests it is really difficult to spot. 
I can check the  OperatingSystem.Version on. FreeBSD. Unlike Linux where you can have kernel and various distributions around it, FreeBSD is really unified OS.  We can also make the Version return what ever we feel is reasonable e.g. 12.x or 13.x in this case. 

Or we can just go with the 13.x flavor and document broken behavior on 12.

> Or we can just go with the 13.x flavor and document broken behavior on 12.

As you like, but I see no problem to maintain both versions. You can assign the issue to me. However, as I said, we need appropriate VMs in DevOps pipeline, because I'm working on Linux and have no chance to test it locally.
@sakno is getting VMs added something I can help out with or is that something that needs to be done internally?

CI machines are not going to happen. (long story) I think ether me or @Thefrank are best sources for testing. 
I test my system and OperatingSystem.Version  returns 13.0.0 "normal" FreeBSD version.
